phase1_eligibility: BLOCKED -- no reproducible, attribution-eligible baseline failure was found. #418 remains blocked. Per #417's own rule, a fake failure must NOT be generated to continue.
falsification_findings: The live Judge reliably distinguished an obvious harmful routing violation from a correct one, order-consistently on verdict -- the 'live Judge cannot distinguish obvious cases / is materially order-biased' falsification criterion did NOT fire.

The harness's subject layer changed behaviour exactly as predicted for a targeted harmful shadow mutation (CAL-2b), and did not for the baseline (CAL-4b) -- the 'no real/reproducible failures can be found or attributed to the mutable surface' criterion is NOT cleared but the mutable surface is demonstrably load-bearing.
CAL-2 shows a control-design pitfall (a deep-rule mutation can be masked by a higher-priority rule); this is a calibration lesson for #418's control selection, not a harness defect.
The v0.1 standing position -- 'no genuine field-observed failure exists yet; manual bounded review currently yields equivalent value' -- still holds: Phase 0 found no baseline failure.
limitations: repo_replay via a fresh non-Project ChatGPT conversation is a lower-fidelity approximation of the real configured AI-OS Project runtime; no UI-equivalence claim is made.
Subject and Judge share a model class (limited_same_model_class); Judge agreement is not independent corroboration.
Token/cost usage is not observable from the browser UI (not_captured / not_observable, never estimated).

Part B used a single run per family (compressed scope). Reproducibility per #395 was not exercised; this is sufficient to conclude no_failure_found but not to certify the harness's repeated-run behaviour.
